sentences.text: Alexander W.A. Kellner named the genus Dawndraco in 2010.
The type species is Dawndraco kanzai, a name honoring the Kanza tribe of Kansas.
Its generic name blends the Dawn deity of the Iroquois with the Latin word for dragon.
The genus relies on holotype specimen UALVP 24238, which preserves a partial skeleton featuring an almost complete skull and lower jaws.
Richard C. Fox and Allen Lindoe recovered the fossil in 1974 from the Niobrara Formation in Utica, Kansas.
Kellner assigned Dawndraco to the family Pteranodontidae.
The rocks containing the fossil date to the late Coniacian or early Santonian stage, approximately 86 million years ago, within a broader range from 89.8 to 83.6 million years ago.

Martin-Silverstone et al. argued that the taxonomic characterizations of Dawndraco were suspect and that the stratigraphic arguments used to distinguish it were questionable. They interpreted the specimen as a small, immature individual of the larger male size class of Pteranodon sternbergi.
